newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Congress debates constitutional judges ouster.
newsitem.headline: Peru Congress debates constitutional judges ouster.

text.p: Peru's Congress held a marathon session Wednesday to debate ousting Constitutional Court judges who rejected a law that would have cleared the way for a third election bid by President Alberto Fujimori.

"I want their suspension, their sacking and a prohibition so that they cannot hold public office for ten years," said Fujimori supporter Enrique Chirinos, who was a member of a congressional commission that investigated the judges.

The commission accused four of the seven judges on the autonomous body of acting improperly when they passed judgment on the reelection law after three members of the court refused to issue a legal interpretation.

If the full Congress, where Fujimori's supporters have a clear majority, were to agree with the commission's findings, government legislators said they would have the right to remove the judges from their posts.
"These people have not committed any wrong and, in fact, the interests of those who want to keep Fujimori in power are really behind this," Valentin Paniagua, a lawyer for the judges, told Congress.
Peruvian law is ambiguous on whether Fujimori, who became president in 1990 and was reelected after rewriting the constitution in 1995, can run for an unprecedented third term in 2000.

Earlier this year, the four accused judges issued two separate rulings on a government-sponsored law designed to allow Fujimori to run again. The two confusing interpretiations over the decision meant the president was left with an insecure legal platform from which to launch his candidacy.
While government legislators said the court ratified their favourable interpretation, the opposition claimed a third election bid would be illegal.
